newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to lure investors with German help.
newsitem.headline: Romania to lure investors with German help.

text.p: Germany's PR consultants Achelis & Partner won a tender launched by Romania's main foreign investment promoter to help the Balkan country advertise its business opportunities worldwide.

The project, with assistance from the European Union's Phare programme, will run for five months on a 400,000 Ecus ($472,000) budget, the Romanian Development Agency said at a news conference on Wednesday.
Achelis & Partner will work with Public Relations Partners, a Belgian PR consultancy company, and the Romanian subsidiary of Britain's consultants Coopers & Lybrand.
"The objective of this project is to give technical assistance to improve communication to promote Romanian economic opportunities," Achelis & Partners president Thomas Achelis said.
He said the project included an evaluation report on existing resources in Romania, editing promotional materials, as well as training courses for local staff.
Total direct foreign investment in Romania since the 1989 end of communism was $2.2 billion at the end of 1996, a paltry figure compared with levels elsewhere in Eastern Europe.
Romania hopes foreign investment will pick up this year as the new centrist government pledged to support foreign investors by boosting facilities, including tax cuts and foreign ownership of land.
